title: I Should Have: Regrets and Reproaches

sections.title: Looking back with a modal
sections.content: You know *deber* and *tener que* from B1 Unit 4: *Deberías llamarla* is advice about now. To look back at the past, keep the modal in the conditional and add *haber* + past participle: *Deberías haber llamado* means "you should have called" (and you did not). Said about yourself it is a regret, said about someone else it is a reproach. *Tendría que haber* works the same way. For a plain regret, use *me arrepiento de* + infinitive; with a past action the infinitive is *haber* + participle: *Me arrepiento de haber dicho eso*.

sections.title: Four ways to look back
rows: Me arrepiento de no haber estudiado más.
I regret not having studied more.

items.spanish: Debería haber salido más temprano; ahora llegamos tarde.
items.english: I should have left earlier; now we are late.

items.spanish: Deberías haber avisado antes de cambiar la hora.
items.english: You should have warned us before changing the time.

items.spanish: Tendríamos que haber reservado la mesa con tiempo.
items.english: We should have booked the table in advance.

items.spanish: Me arrepiento de haber dicho eso.

sections.content: Compare *Deberías llamar* (advice: you should call, now) with *Deberías haber llamado* (a reproach: you did not). Only *haber* carries the past: the modal stays *debería* or *tendría que*, and the participle never changes: *haber llamado*.
